subject: [PATCH v4 0/7] sched/numa: stop VMA scan filters from gating promotion

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary: Reviewer David suggested simplifying the patch by removing the need to pass the vma pointer, as it can be obtained from vma->vm_mm
reviews.raw_body:
mm can be had from vma->vm_mm, so likely sufficient to only pass the vma?

Apart from that this looks much clearer to me

ack. agreed.

If nothing else comes up on v4, could you please fold the fixlet below?

--- >8 ---

Subject: sched/numa: drop mm argument from vma_needs_placement_scan()

The mm can be had from vma->vm_mm.
---
 kernel/sched/fair.c | 6 +++---
 1 file changed, 3 insertions(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/kernel/sched/fair.c b/kernel/sched/fair.c
index 3b30786ded3b..095289d3da3c 100644
--- a/kernel/sched/fair.c
+++ b/kernel/sched/fair.c
@@ -4082,9 +4082,9 @@ static void reset_ptenuma_scan(struct task_struct *p)
 	p->mm->numa_scan_offset = 0;
 }
 
-static bool vma_needs_placement_scan(struct mm_struct *mm,
-		struct vm_area_struct *vma)
+static bool vma_needs_placement_scan(struct vm_area_struct *vma)
 {
+	struct mm_struct *mm = vma->vm_mm;
 	unsigned long pids;
 	/*
 	 * Allow unconditional access first two times, so that all the (pages)
@@ -4313,7 +4313,7 @@ static void task_numa_work(struct callback_head *work)
 		 * VMA candidate exists. If a scan is already in-progress, finish it,
 		 * but track continuation separately from starting a new one.
 		 */
-		placement_due = vma_needs_placement_scan(mm, vma);
+		placement_due = vma_needs_placement_scan(vma);
 		scan_started = mm->numa_scan_offset > vma->vm_start;
 		pid_scan_allowed = vma_pids_forced || placement_due;

2026-10-01.patch_summary: This patch series addresses poor NUMA balancing behavior in a production deployment by modifying the VMA scan filters to no longer gate memory-tier promotion. The issue arises from the global balancing mode's inability to describe the intent of individual VMA/PTE walks, leading to suboptimal performance and high request latency. To resolve this, the patch series introduces promotion-only NUMA protection walks and derives private VMA state in the folio eligibility check. It also separates VMA placement eligibility from partial-scan continuation and scans PID-inactive VMAs for promotion. The patches are designed to be backportable and include cleanups of the touched NUMA-balancing code.
